entries.title: How Gemini plans such detailed vacation itineraries for you
entries.content:
Planning a trip can feel like a second job. Between hunting down flight confirmations, mapping distances between destinations, and scrolling through countless restaurant reviews, the logistics quickly stack up. Gemini can take some of that work off your plate, helping you organize custom vacations with less stress. All you need to do is ask.

Gemini doesn’t just browse the web — it connects directly to Google Maps, Hotels, and Flights to build highly personalized itineraries based on real-world data and your specific preferences. Here’s what happens behind the scenes when you ask it for help planning a trip, whether you’re brainstorming options or finalizing bookings.

Gathering real-time data

Let’s say you’re taking a trip to Kyoto later this year. You need flights, hotels, and restaurant reservations — plus stuff to do while you’re there. Gemini first tackles this challenge by tapping into Google’s ecosystem for accurate, real-world data.

Gemini gets real-time information — think locations, reviews, prices, and more — from Google Maps, Flights, and Hotels. It also pulls visual inspiration and recommendations from YouTube creators. And if you call on the Viator app while you’re in Gemini, it can even help you explore and book expertly curated travel tours, activities, and excursions.

Finding the best recommendations

Gemini then pairs that Google Search data with advanced AI to give you custom travel recommendations.

Gemini uses the context you’ve provided in your prompt — including basics, like your destination and travel dates, or specifics, like that you’re looking for hidden-gem brunch spots near the train station. And if you toggle on Personal Intelligence in Google apps — like Gmail, Photos, Search, and YouTube — Gemini can proactively factor in your interests, preferences, and constraints.

With Personal Intelligence, Gemini securely connects the dots across your Google apps, past chats, and custom instructions. It can make personalized suggestions, like restaurants to try based on food pictures you’ve saved to Google Photos or travel videos you’ve searched on YouTube. It can also reference plans you’ve already booked using flight details, hotel confirmations, and restaurant reservations in your Gmail.

If you ask Gemini to remember your interests and past picks, it can help you find new favorites fine-tuned to your tastes. It can even identify patterns across your Google apps to recommend your next perfect travel destination.

Building your itinerary

Gemini understands how different trip requirements — like locations, travel times, existing plans, and personal preferences — intersect. So when you ask it to build an itinerary, it creates a cohesive plan that accounts for all your constraints.

Gemini can create custom routes and group things to do by neighborhood. And with Personal Intelligence, it can build your itinerary around your existing plans and preferences — cross-referencing times and locations before weaving things into your schedule.

Gemini Spark, your 24/7 personal AI agent, can also make sense of your inbox — turning messy trip-planning email chains into a clear master plan. Ask it to monitor your Gmail, and as items related to your trip (like booked tours, flights, and hotels) pop up, it works in the background — automatically building out a Google Doc with your travel itinerary.

Finalizing the details

Gemini doesn’t stop at building itineraries. It can handle the heavy lifting and help you finalize the details of your trip.

Gemini Spark, for example, can help with mundane tasks, like comparing rental cars or drafting a packing list. It handles the research, saving you the tedium of juggling multiple tabs or obsessively checking the weather. When it’s done, it suggests the best choices and lets you make the final decision.

Gemini Spark can also even use Chrome to navigate to your favorite airline’s site, search for flights, and start filling in your booking information — handing the task back over to you, so all you have to do is press “book.” It can also help you find and book travel accommodations and manage dining reservations. And if you give it access, it can email your finalized itinerary to your travel crew so everyone knows the plan.

entries.title: Parents can now send money to their kids on Google Wallet.
entries.summary: U.S. parents can set up a secure digital balance on Google Wallet for their kids to tap and pay using Android and Wear OS devices.
entries.content:
With back-to-school season fast approaching, parents are busy preparing their children for the year ahead. To make getting ready a little easier, today we're launching a new Google Wallet tool that gives parents a safe and simple way to manage their kids' money, building on the helpful features we already offer to families.

Now parents in the U.S. can set up a secure balance on Google Wallet for their children and teens under 18. In an increasingly cashless world, kids can tap to pay with Google Pay in stores using their NFC-enabled Android or Wear OS devices.

As a parent, you have full control of their balance and activity through Family Link. You can easily transfer money directly from your own account, and soon you'll be able to schedule automated regular payments. You can also set specific spending limits and track transactions in real time. And if needed, you can lock or unlock the balance instantly. It's a practical way to teach children smart money habits and give them independence, all without needing to open a bank account.

entries.title: Our WeatherNext 2 AI model demonstrated a massive leap forward in predicting cyclones.
entries.summary: Google DeepMind’s WeatherNext 2 shows state-of-the-art accuracy in cyclone prediction.
entries.content:
Predicting how hurricanes and cyclones develop is a longstanding challenge, and every hour of warning counts. Tropical cyclones are among the most destructive weather events on Earth, and for meteorologists, issuing accurate, timely warnings is a constant race against time.

Today, in a paper published in Nature, Google researchers show that our WeatherNext AI model achieved state-of-the-art accuracy in predicting a cyclone's track, intensity, and wind structure. This represents a massive leap forward — roughly a decade of meteorological progress in one model.

To help build climate resilience worldwide, we are now open-sourcing the WeatherNext 2 model to the global research community. For more information, check the Google DeepMind blog.

entries.title: Step into the world of tango on Google Arts & Culture
entries.content:
Journey into the heart of one of Argentina’s most passionate and iconic cultural treasures: tango. Through a new collection on Google Arts & Culture, we’re bringing the history, music, and spirit of tango to users around the world.

Google Arts & Culture has long been committed to preserving and celebrating Argentina’s rich heritage, having collaborated with 25 local partners across the country. Following the success of Argentina’s Table — our exploration of the nation’s diverse culinary scene — we’re now turning our focus to the dance and music style that’s captivated global audiences and earned a place on UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage list.

In collaboration with five key partners — MALBA (Museo de Arte Latinoamericano de Buenos Aires Malba), Tango & Tango, The National Secretariat of Culture of Argentina, the Ministry of Culture of the City of Buenos Aires, and Marca País Argentina — we’ve brought together over 50 stories, not just about the dance, but about the people who keep it alive. Visit the collection to explore the legacies of legends like Carlos Gardel and Julio De Caro, as well as the personal stories of contemporary orchestra players, passionate dancers, and the artisans who craft the instruments and shoes that define the tango style.

"In the national government, we celebrate initiatives like this, which combine technology, cooperation between institutions, and coordination with the private sector to preserve and disseminate our cultural heritage," says Leonardo Cifelli, Argentina's national secretary of culture. "A few weeks away from a new anniversary of tango’s UNESCO recognition (September 30), this collaboration represents a new opportunity to project one of the most valuable expressions of Argentine identity to the world."

Born in the barrios: Tango rose from humble beginnings to global fame. Its journey reflects Argentina's own evolution, embracing both its heritage and its future. This cultural weight that ultimately led to tango’s 2009 inclusion on UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage list, cementing its place as a pillar of global identity despite ongoing debates over its institutionalization.

The legends of tango: The genre was shaped by iconic master musicians like Carlos Gardel, Ástor Piazzolla, Aníbal Troilo, Julio De Caro and other tango figures, whose enduring legacies still define the rhythm and soul of the music today.

A global heartbeat in Buenos Aires: A powerful global attraction, tango brings people from all corners of the world to the streets of Buenos Aires, uniting a passionate international community. Discover how this comes to life throughout the city by exploring tango neighborhoods and learning about the historic traditions of tango bars.

Whether you’re a seasoned milonguero or discovering tango for the first time, we hope this project inspires you to step into the history, movement and soul of Argentina on the dedicated page and by downloading the free Google Arts & Culture app on iOS or Android.

entries.title: Ask Maps gets more helpful with food ordering and more
entries.content:
Ask Maps is Google Maps’ biggest transformation in over a decade. By bringing Gemini model capabilities together with the world’s freshest map, we’ve made it easier than ever to get answers to real-world questions.

We’ve been thrilled to see how Ask Maps is helping people use Maps in entirely new ways — from finding a restaurant with great vibes that’s still quiet enough for conversation to mapping out a scenic three-hour motorcycle ride. Building on this, we’re now making Ask Maps even more helpful with new agentic capabilities, real-time transit information, Personal Intelligence, and conversational contributions so you can get more done. It’s also rolling out in Australia, Brazil, Canada, Indonesia, Japan, and Mexico, along with over 150 countries and territories in English.

Order food, find the perfect hotel, and discover events.

Ask Maps can now handle complex, multi-step tasks for you using new agentic capabilities. If you want to order takeout before leaving the office, just ask Maps to “order spicy pad kee mao with seafood for me to pick up on my way home.” It’ll find open restaurants along your route that serve what you're craving and can even consider things like your saved places or specific dietary needs. Once you select a restaurant, Ask Maps can automatically add the dish you’re looking for directly to your cart so you can easily review and complete your order. Food ordering is rolling out now with partners like Square and Toast, with Uber Eats coming soon. We’ll continue to evolve these experiences as we co-develop the Universal Commerce Protocol for Food with partners.

With Ask Maps, you can also quickly discover the latest information about hotels and local events. Ask for what you need: “For next week’s conference in downtown Miami, find me a decently priced, top-rated hotel with an artsy vibe, within walking distance from a gym and restaurants.” Ask Maps compares real-time prices and checks availability for you so you can find the right spot. And if you need ideas for what to do nearby, Ask Maps will show you everything from concerts to comedy shows, complete with links for tickets.

Get personalized answers and resume past conversations.

With Personal Intelligence, you can choose to securely connect Ask Maps to Gmail, and soon other apps like Calendar. Ask Maps automatically factors in your upcoming flight or dinner reservations, giving you relevant suggestions without you having to explain your existing plans. For example, if you’re traveling, try asking: “Give me ideas on how to spend a few hours near the hotel before my flight tomorrow.” You'll see nearby recommendations based on your hotel reservation in Gmail — along with tips for getting to the airport afterwards, like what time to leave.

With Personal Intelligence in Ask Maps, you’re in control — connecting to your Gmail is off by default and you decide if you want to connect. Personal Intelligence is built with privacy in mind, and you can learn more about our approach here.

If your history settings are turned on, Ask Maps also remembers past conversations so you can pick up where you left off. Simply ask, “Remind me, what activities did you suggest for my trip to Seattle?” Maps will instantly pull up your previous ideas so you don't have to start planning from scratch.

Get trusted, real-time transit information instantly.

Ask Maps already gives you helpful, real-time information — like what traffic to expect on your morning commute or if there’s construction or an accident along the way. You can even check how busy a shop or restaurant is before you head out so you can avoid waiting in long lines. Now, we’re bringing these live updates to transit. A new transit widget right in Ask Maps keeps you informed about up-to-the-minute delays for your bus, train, subway, or ferry ride. So if you ask, “Is there a ferry to get to Taronga Zoo with views of the Opera House?” you’ll see all of your options at a glance on a virtual departure board. If a ferry is running late, the wait adjusts in real-time — updating minute by minute — so you know exactly when to head to the dock.

Tell Maps about updates and share tips conversationally

Insights from over 500 million contributors play a big role in keeping Maps fresh and helpful, and now we’re making it simpler to share updates. You can suggest edits conversationally, right from Ask Maps and the Contribute tab. You can even upload a photo of a storefront sign — Maps will detect the new hours from the image, and ask you to confirm before submitting the suggestion for you. As always, Maps’ built-in protection systems review suggested edits for accuracy, and won’t post suggestions that violate our policies. It’s also easy to tell Maps about an insider tip — just say something like “more parking is available behind the building,” and Ask Maps will surface this helpful information to others in the community.

The live transit widget, more personalized responses, and remembering past conversations in Ask Maps are rolling out now everywhere Ask Maps is available. Food ordering, discovering hotels and events, and conversational contributions are rolling out now in the U.S., with more countries to come over time. With these updates, we hope Ask Maps makes navigating your day just a little easier.

entries.title: The next chapter of our AI momentum
entries.summary: Today, Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai shared some changes with Google DeepMind teams.
entries.content:
Editor’s note: Today, Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai shared some changes with Google DeepMind teams, including new roles for Demis Hassabis and Koray Kavukcuoglu. Below are the messages Sundar and Demis sent to employees.

Message from Sundar Pichai

We’ve made extraordinary progress to deliver on our full AI stack. We’ve got amazing talent, world-class compute, and products that bring AI to more people than any other company. And you saw the incredible momentum at earnings across all our businesses, including Search, YouTube, and Cloud. Our Gemini models are in high demand among developers and businesses, and the Gemini app reached 950M+ monthly users. Meanwhile, our AI research continues to drive field-defining breakthroughs (like last week’s Gemini Robotics advances).

We have to accelerate all this work and stay focused on the AI frontier. At the same time, there’s never been a more important moment to shape the future of AGI and science. Today Demis, Koray and I are sharing a few changes to our Google DeepMind teams that will enable us to do both.

AGI and science: Demis has described us as standing in the foothills of the singularity, and has been spending a lot of his time engaging externally. He and I have been long discussing a role that allows him to put his full attention on actively shaping the future of AGI. It’s work that is vitally important to Alphabet and humanity, and I can’t imagine a better person than Demis to do it. So, moving forward, Demis will become the Chair of GDM and Chief Scientist of Alphabet, while continuing to lead Isomorphic Labs. He’ll remain closely connected to Koray, Josh, and our GDM teams, advising across models and research. I’m so excited for Demis — this is truly his life’s work and purpose. You can read Demis’s note to GDM below.

Google DeepMind: We are building strong momentum: Flash is in high demand, our Cyber model is live, and Gemma models have surpassed 900M+ downloads. We are committed to being at the frontier, and are super focused on the areas where we need to improve. I’m really excited for our upcoming model releases and the progress we’re seeing. We have to continue to move fast and with clear purpose here. Koray, the current Chief Technology Officer of GDM and our Chief AI Architect, will step up as SVP of Google DeepMind, reporting to me. He will oversee Gemini model development, Frontier AI research, and the Gemini app and developer teams. Koray has been at DeepMind since its early days, and over his 13 years there, he has started our deep learning team and led the way on breakthroughs like WaveNet and DQN. I look forward to seeing him lead GDM into this next chapter.

Lastly, after an incredible 27-year run, Jeff Dean is at a moment where he wants to try something new, and we’re excited to support him in that. Jeff and Google Senior Fellow Sanjay Ghemawat are launching an independent public benefit corporation to accelerate discoveries in ML, science, and engineering. Jeff and Sanjay helped to drive some of the most significant technology transitions, from our early search infrastructure to the neural networks that helped create the modern AI era. On a personal note, it’s been a privilege to work alongside Jeff and Sanjay, and I wish them all the best! We’ll continue to work with them as a founding investor and Cloud partner, and collaborate on a research framework for ML systems and related infrastructure advances.

We are at a dynamic moment with so much opportunity ahead. With today's changes we're going to keep driving our momentum. Onwards!

-Sundar

Message from Demis Hassabis

Hi Team

We have arrived at a pivotal moment in human history. I’ve been working towards AGI my whole life and now, like many of you, I feel it is close at hand. It’s critical that we collectively get the next steps right to ensure this all goes well for humanity and we usher in an incredible new age of discovery and wonder.

With this backdrop, I’ve decided that now is the right time for me to hand over my day-to-day operational responsibilities at GDM, so that I have the time and space to focus on the big picture and help influence what is to come to the best of my ability. I will be taking on a new strategic role as Chair of GDM and Chief Scientist of Alphabet, and I’m excited to announce that Koray will be stepping up to lead GDM as SVP of Google DeepMind, in addition to his role as Chief AI Architect of Google.

Koray and I have been working together for over 13 years, since the early days of DeepMind. He is one of the world's foremost AI experts and has been championing GDM's mission from day one. I have total confidence in Koray, Josh, and the rest of the GDM exec team as they continue to spearhead the latest AI developments across Google. The Gemini models are in good hands with Koray and the leads, as they have been for a while, and I'm excited about the great progress we’re making with our new models including Gemini 4.

In my new role, I will continue to work closely with Sundar on strategic and global AGI matters, and to advise Koray, Josh, and the GDM leads, from our awesome new London Platform 37 offices. As part of this transition, I’ll also be leaning into my role at Isomorphic, where we are making extremely rapid and promising progress, to accelerate our mission there even faster. As you've heard me say many times, I’ve always believed the No.1 application of AI should be to improve human health. It’s time for AI to prove its unequivocal value to the world, and what better way to demonstrate that than to help finally cure diseases like cancer.

We’ve built a unique culture at GDM that has served us very well. I want to thank each and every one of you for your brilliance, dedication, and effort that make GDM the huge success it is today. We should all be extremely proud of the amazing things we’ve achieved so far. We’ve become the AI engine room of Google, with Gemini delivering helpful experiences everywhere including AI Mode and AI Overviews, the Gemini App rocketing to over 950M monthly users, and our fundamental and scientific research continues to lead the world. I’m very excited for our next chapter and the best is yet to come!

As a business we are in an incredibly strong position. We are the only company that has the full stack and we’re world-class at every layer from infrastructure to cloud to frontier models to AI-first applications. We have all the ingredients to lead from here, and I firmly believe we will.

Best

Demis

entries.title: The latest AI news we announced in July 2026
entries.content:
For more than 20 years, we’ve invested in machine learning and AI research, tools, and infrastructure to build products that make everyday life better for more people. Teams across Google are working on ways to unlock AI’s benefits in fields as wide-ranging as healthcare, crisis response, and education. To keep you posted on our progress, we're doing a regular roundup of Google's most recent AI news.

Here’s a look back at some of our AI announcements from July.

July brought a wave of AI advances to support developers, simplify everyday life, and protect local communities. We gave developers faster, more efficient Gemini models for scaling production agents and advancing robotics. We also expanded our creative suite with next-generation music and video tools, and made Search and Gemini Spark even more connected to your go-to daily apps. Plus, we announced a new skilled trades alliance and new satellites for early wildfire detection — and Google DeepMind Co-Founder and CEO Demis Hassabis shared his vision for this critical moment in history. Together, our July updates showed how AI can be more practical, creative, and helpful than ever before.

Check out three new Gemini models. Developers and customers building production AI agents need higher token efficiency, lower latency, and more reliable performance. Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and 3.5 Flash Cyber are built to meet the sweet spot of efficiency and quality to enable scaling agentic workflows.

See how robots gear up with Gemini Robotics ER 2. We launched Gemini Robotics ER 2, our most capable "embodied reasoning" model yet. Built for developers crafting genuinely helpful machines, ER 2 bridges the gap between digital smarts and the physical world. It lets systems chat naturally with people, make sense of their surroundings, and work through complex, multi-step tasks.

Get started with Gemini Intelligence on the latest devices from Galaxy Unpacked 2026. With the launch of the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Fold8, and Flip8, we’re making it easier than ever to get started on Android while also rolling out the first capabilities of Gemini Intelligence. 1

Switch to Android even more easily and bring your data with you. With the launch of Samsung’s new Z Series at Galaxy Unpacked, we introduced a new native migration experience built directly into Android 17 that lets you transfer even more data types from an iPhone wirelessly — without downloading a separate app.

Streamline your research with Gemini Notebook. Gemini Notebook is the same standalone product as the hugely popular NotebookLM, only now it's doing more across the Google ecosystem — including inside the Gemini app and Google Search — and it’s updated with a secure cloud computer.

Explore the first iteration of the AI & Economy ATLAS. Google’s ATLAS is an expansive look at how people are using AI at work and in day-to-day life. This ongoing, large-scale, de-identified study is designed to offer an early view of a quickly moving landscape: AI’s capabilities are advancing, its use is evolving, and tools for observing its impact on the economy are still a work-in-progress.

Meet the Alliance for America’s Skilled Trades. To help meet the growing demand for skilled trades workers, we’re joining forces with BlackRock, Carhartt, and Ford to launch the Alliance for America’s Skilled Trades. Together, we’ll build a stronger pipeline for the skilled trades, scale evidence-based training approaches, and expand opportunities nationwide through cross-industry partnerships.

See how AlphaEvolve can help Cloud customers solve their hardest problems. Finding the most efficient algorithm can be challenging. To help, we made AlphaEvolve, our Gemini-powered AI code-optimization agent, generally available to all Google Cloud customers on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. AlphaEvolve acts as an evolutionary collaborator: You provide a baseline algorithm and your goals, and it automatically searches for better solutions, returning human-readable, optimized code.

Connect more of your apps to Search. You can already connect some of your favorite services to the Gemini app. To help you get even more done, we’re enabling you to securely link and interact with your go-to apps like YouTube Music directly in AI Mode.

With Personal Intelligence and your connected apps, Search can give even more tailored responses.

Handle complex web errands with Gemini Spark. We expanded Gemini Spark to more users around the world, and added a new feature to help you handle complex web errands. Now, with your permission, Spark can use your logged-in accounts and saved passwords to handle tedious web errands, like scheduling viewings for apartments or researching flight options and starting the booking process.

Create and personalize your videos in Google Vids with new updates. Two new features — Gemini Omni and personal avatars — make video creation easier than ever. Now you can generate and edit high-quality clips using everyday language, and create a custom digital avatar to star in your videos.

See how we reconstructed Pelé’s “lost” goal. On August 2, 1959, Pelé scored the most beautiful goal of his career: three consecutive “sombreros” over defenders and the goalkeeper without the ball ever touching the ground. But the moment was never captured on film. We used Google DeepMind technology to reconstruct a lost piece of football history and tell the story of how it all came to life.

Celebrate 25 years of visual search innovation with new features. It’s been 25 years since we launched Google Images, beginning the evolution of Search from a text-based experience to one that allows you to visually explore the world. To celebrate, we announced a new browseable home for Google Images and image generation through AI Overviews in Search. We also looked back at the major launches that transformed how we search with — and for — images.

Make music with the newest music generation model, Lyria 3.5. Google Flow Music helps you create songs you love with total creative control. Powered by our latest Lyria 3.5 model, it delivers significant advancements in musicality, lyrics, and vocal quality to help you craft richer tracks.

See how NOAA and Google Cloud are advancing weather forecasting. NOAA (National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration) is modernizing its operational supercomputing system by using Google Cloud’s high-performance H4D virtual machines to run its atmospheric models. As one of the first organizations to bring numerical weather prediction directly to the public cloud, NOAA provides meteorologists with the scale, speed, and AI capabilities needed to run massive simulations and deliver faster, life-saving early warnings.

Learn how AI breakthroughs can help people prepare for and respond to natural hazards. With the release of the UN report “Leveraging AI to enhance multi-hazard early warning systems,” we shared how our teams at Google support crisis resilience efforts with advanced AI-based breakthroughs, detection, and forecasting — while working with partners to make timely information available to billions of people. Our goal is a world where no one is surprised by a natural disaster.

Discover how three new satellites joined the fight against wildfires. Three new FireSat satellites successfully launched from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California, expanding a global initiative led by the Earth Fire Alliance (EFA) with Google Research to help detect wildfires before they spread.

Examine the bioresilience program designed to protect global communities. Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs shared a joint approach to bioresilience. The goal is twofold: to prevent threat actors from misusing our models, and to ensure that governments, scientists, biosecurity experts and our teams can harness these technologies to build a more resilient world.

entries.title: Welcome to Sail Tower, our newest Austin office
entries.content:
We’ve been a proud part of the Austin community for nearly 20 years, moving from our first campus in North Austin to our current one downtown and growing to thousands of employees. And now, we’re deepening our commitment to the Lone Star State with our newest office and Google.org nonprofit venue at Sail Tower.

Located in the heart of the city, this iconic sail-shaped building is a celebration of Texas culture, greeting Googlers with bright colors and local artwork. We’ve designed each floor around a different Texas region, paying homage to the desert wildflowers of Big Bend, the hiking trails of Hill Country, and the thunderstorms of Marfa. The workspace also provides a variety of flexible areas for collaboration, innovation, and focused work, including outdoor terraces with native Texas plants and inspiring views.

Beyond serving as a new home for Googlers, Sail Tower will also welcome in the Austin community. We’re opening a new Google.org venue for nonprofit programming, and local (Austin metro area) nonprofits can book the space for board meetings, workshops, classes, and community events at no cost. Learn more.

“Spaces like this are absolutely vital for Austin’s nonprofit community,” said Austin Mayor Kirk Watson. “When good neighbors and partners like Google open doors to our local visionaries, they’re not just offering a physical space, they’re strengthening the fabric of Austin and helping our community thrive.”

We’re excited for Sail Tower to become a hub for connection and technological advancement in Austin for years to come.

entries.title: Inside our 353,000-person vibe coding course
entries.summary: Illustrations of a laptop, an AI spark, messages, code, and a 3-D cube
entries.content:
AI is moving faster than traditional methods of learning and teaching can keep up with it. With new concepts, skills, ideas, and tools arriving almost daily, we needed a new way to teach and learn these new technologies.

Since Google and Kaggle’s first “5 Day Intensive” course in 2024 more than 2 million learners and developers have participated in the multimodal, no cost courses. Our latest collaboration, the 5-Day AI Agents: Intensive Vibe Coding Course with Google, had over 353,000 registered participants. Together, we explored the frontier of vibe coding, where people program through natural language. Our courses navigated the entire lifecycle of designing, securing, and deploying production-grade AI agents in the cloud. The response proved that developers are ready to graduate their prototypes "from vibe to live”.

Hundreds of thousands of learners gathered across codelabs and technical whitepapers to collaborate in real time. The heart of this collaboration was on Kaggle's Discord, where over 392,000 active participants swapped code, debugged together, and formed study groups.

The capstone projects brought the week’s learning into action. We received over 6,000 project submissions from more than 12,000 active capstone participants.

The projects demonstrated the immense creativity, technical skill, and imagination of the global AI developer community. From advanced digital humanities tools like the historical manuscript transcription pipeline Palimpsest, to sophisticated space-weather research systems like Project ARIES, the caliber of submissions made it incredibly difficult to narrow down the top entries. You can explore all the winning teams and their capstone projects on our website.

We look forward to continuing our partnership and exploring future learning opportunities. If you’re interested in learning more, you can continue honing your skills through ongoing Kaggle competitions and stay connected with fellow learners on the Kaggle Discord. For those who missed the live event in June but still want to learn, all course content remains available as a self-paced Kaggle Learn guide.

entries.title: Simplify your morning with this vibe-coded schedule app.
entries.summary: Tired of starting your morning staring at bright screens and stressful notifications? Raph, a creative technologist at Google, built a custom app called Glanceboard with…
entries.content:
Tired of starting your morning staring at bright screens and stressful notifications? Raph, a creative technologist at Google, built a custom app called Glanceboard with Gemini 3.6 Flash and Nano Banana to transform that daily routine.

Every morning, Glanceboard checks Raph’s family Google Calendar and the local weather. Then, it prompts Nana Banana to generate a personalized illustration of his children wearing forecast-friendly clothes. That image shows up on an e-ink display, letting Raphael’s family know their schedule, what to wear, and what to pack for the day.

Glanceboard operates on a lightweight local server — no cloud accounts or bright screens required — offering a serene and personalized way to stay organized. And Raphael says it’s a great way to get kids engaged and organized without the stress.

Want to try Glanceboard yourself? We’re open-sourcing the code so you can ask Google Antigravity to make you one, too. Get the full details on how to build it and the hardware he used in the GitHub repo.
